# saisdata

<!-- badges: start -->
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/Teal-Insights/saisdata/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/Teal-Insights/saisdata/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![r-universe](https://teal-insights.r-universe.dev/saisdata/badges/version)](https://teal-insights.r-universe.dev/saisdata)
[![Website](https://github.com/Teal-Insights/saisdata/actions/workflows/pkgdown.yaml/badge.svg)](https://teal-insights.github.io/saisdata/)
[![Code license: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/code%20license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE.md)
[![Data terms: IMF and World Bank](https://img.shields.io/badge/data%20terms-IMF%20and%20World%20Bank-lightgrey.svg)](LICENSE-data.md)
<!-- badges: end -->

`saisdata` holds the course data for the two-day R workshop of the Master of International Economics and Finance (MIEF) at Johns Hopkins SAIS, ready to use in R. One line loads everything: `library(saisdata)`. There are no file paths, no downloads and no CSV files to read.

This package is not an official IMF or World Bank product.

## Installation

Run this one line in the R Console:

```r
install.packages("saisdata", repos = "https://teal-insights.r-universe.dev")
```

You do not need a GitHub account, devtools, a compiler or a manual download. The package holds only data and depends on no other package, so that one repository is all R needs.

## What is inside

| Dataset | What one row is | Rows | Help page |
|---|---|---|---|
| `weo` | one country (or IMF group) in one year, 2000 to 2031: gross debt, primary balance, overall balance, GDP | 6,720 | `?weo` |
| `weo_groups` | one IMF country group and one indicator, with the years across, the way the IMF publishes it | 6 | `?weo_groups` |
| `wb_groups` | one country, with its World Bank region, income level and lending type | 217 | `?wb_groups` |

`weo` and `weo_groups` come from the IMF's World Economic Outlook database of October 2026. `wb_groups` comes from the World Bank, as served on 3 November 2026. The tables are a frozen snapshot: they do not change when either institution publishes new numbers. Every help page says what each column means, the units, the source and what was changed.

The data arrive as tibbles if you have the tidyverse, and print as ordinary data frames if you do not.

## Example

This runs offline. It uses only base R, so it works in a brand new R library. Net interest is not a column; it is the primary balance minus the overall balance.

```{r kenya}
library(saisdata)

kenya <- subset(weo, code == "KEN" & year >= 2020 & year <= 2025)
kenya$net_interest <- kenya$primary_balance - kenya$overall_balance

as.data.frame(kenya[, c("year", "gross_debt", "net_interest")])
```

With the tidyverse, two moves make `weo_groups` tidy, and one more gives the interest bill in dollars. Added up over the two groups, that comes to about USD 849 billion in 2001 and USD 2,371.2 billion in 2025. The [Getting Started article](https://teal-insights.github.io/saisdata/articles/saisdata.html) has this example and a chart.

```{r tidy, message = FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

weo_groups |>
  select(-indicator_name, -units) |> # keep the codes, drop the long text
  pivot_longer(
    cols = `2001`:`2031`, # every year column
    names_to = "year", # the column names become a year column
    names_transform = as.integer, # "2025" becomes the number 2025
    values_to = "value"
  ) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = indicator, values_from = value) |> # one per indicator
  mutate(net_interest_usd_bn = (GGXONLB_NGDP - GGXCNL_NGDP) * NGDPD / 100)
```

## Code license and data terms

The code and the data are under different terms.

- **The package's code and documentation** are MIT licensed ([`LICENSE.md`](LICENSE.md)). That license does not cover the data.
- **The IMF's data** (`weo`, `weo_groups`) are under the special terms for statistical data on the IMF's [Copyright and Usage page](https://www.imf.org/en/About/copyright-and-terms). You may copy, publish, distribute and build on them if you credit the IMF, keep them accurate and say when you have materially transformed them. For any potential commercial reuse, ask copyright@imf.org first.
- **The World Bank's data** (`wb_groups`) are under [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) with the added terms in its [Terms of Use for Datasets](https://www.worldbank.org/ext/en/legal/terms-conditions/datasets). You may copy, share and adapt them, commercially too, if you credit the World Bank and say what you changed.

[`LICENSE-data.md`](LICENSE-data.md) summarizes both sets of terms, what this package changed in the data, and what you must do if you pass the data on. Once the package is installed, `system.file("LICENSE-data.md", package = "saisdata")` finds the same file.

Print this line under every chart you make from these data:

> Source: International Monetary Fund, World Economic Outlook Database, October 2026, https://data.imf.org/en/datasets/IMF.RES:WEO. Country groups: The World Bank: World Development Indicators: country and lending groups (CC BY 4.0). Net interest is the primary balance minus the overall balance, calculated for this workshop.

Drop the second sentence if your chart uses no World Bank groups, and the third if it shows no net interest.

## Rebuilding the data

A clean clone rebuilds `data/` with no internet. From the package folder, with readr, dplyr, tidyr, stringr, here and usethis installed:

```sh
LANG=en_US.UTF-8 Rscript data-raw/rebuild-all.R
LANG=en_US.UTF-8 Rscript data-raw/compare-tables.R
```

The first line runs the scripts in `data-raw/`, from the source files in [`data-raw/source/`](data-raw/source/README.md). The second compares the result with the original tables, using `identical()`, `all.equal()` and a column-by-column type check, and fails if they differ. The output of the comparison made for this release is in [`data-raw/comparison/`](data-raw/comparison/).
